title: M7: run the comparison and commit the results
description: docs/11 definition of done: model comparison results land in evals/results/ and are committed, so comparisons are part of the repo's history. This is the project's central research output — with only local models available, choosing the model is the only lever left (docs/05).
acceptance_criteria: evals/results/ contains a real multi-model comparison, committed.

title: M7: in-browser evals runner page
description: docs/04 and docs/11: a separate extension page that creates its own engine and runs the labelled policy fixtures against a chosen model. Node cannot drive WebGPU, so this is the only place a real comparison can happen.
acceptance_criteria: The page runs a model over both fixtures and emits a result document.

title: M7: eval scoring against the labelled fixtures
description: docs/05 evals: recall of labelled clauses, precision measured as the share of extracted quotes that verify, schema adherence rate, tokens, wall time. Pure core so it is testable without a browser; scoreAgainstLabels already exists and needs the rest built around it.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring a known-good and a known-bad extraction produces the expected numbers.

title: M7: trace view
description: docs/09 calls this the main research payoff and says to make it good. Step by step through model and tool calls with token usage and timings, showing what the model was asked and what it chose. It gets a full page because a side panel could not do it justice.
acceptance_criteria: A stored trace renders every step with its cost, and what the agent decided is legible without reading JSON.

title: M7: workbench tab shell with dashboard and history
description: docs/09: a full extension page reading the same IndexedDB the side panel writes. Recent audits by site with severity counts, and all audits for a host. It runs no audits and loads no engine.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the workbench lists stored audits and their severity counts.

title: M6: orchestrator and the JSON action protocol
description: docs/06: think-act-observe over response_format, which is the only tool-calling path — S2 found WebLLM injects tools into the prompt rather than constraining them, so supportsToolCalls is false. Invalid tool input is returned to the model as an error rather than crashing the run. finish is the only early exit; maxSteps also ends it.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded run completes within budget; an invalid action is corrected rather than fatal.

title: M6: prompt-injection fixtures
description: docs/06 and docs/11: policy pages containing instructions aimed at the model. Assert the recorded tool-call sequence is unchanged versus a clean run. The stronger claim to test is the mechanism rather than the outcome: the model never sees raw policy text, only schema-validated extractions, so injected instructions should never appear in the orchestrator's message history at all.
acceptance_criteria: Injected text never reaches the message history, and the tool sequence is identical to the clean run.

title: M6: the seven tools
description: docs/06: fetchHeaders, runAnalyzers, discoverPolicies, analyzePolicies, explainFinding, lookupDomain, finish. Network tools check the allowed-domain list themselves before any request, and the worker checks again on its own authority (docs/12 T2). Results are summarised before going back to the model — full results live in the store.
acceptance_criteria: Each tool validates its input, respects the budget, and returns a summary rather than raw JSON.

title: M6: AuditTrace
description: docs/06: every model call and tool call recorded with timings and usage, plus budget consumed. Stored with the audit and replayable. This is the main research payoff (docs/09).
acceptance_criteria: A completed run produces a trace that validates, and replaying it reproduces the same tool sequence.

title: M6: Tool interface, Budget and BudgetTracker
description: docs/06: Tool with name/description/input schema/run/sideEffects, ToolContext, Budget and a tracker that throws BudgetExceeded. Budgets are constructor arguments and defaults are derived from provider.capabilities() and the S2 throughput numbers, not hardcoded (hard rule 5).
acceptance_criteria: A network tool past its fetch budget throws BudgetExceeded before making a request; defaults change with the model's context window.

title: M5: readable-text extraction as a capability
description: docs/05 stage 3 assumed core would run @mozilla/readability and turndown itself, but both need a real DOM and core has no DOM types (hard rule 1). Extraction becomes a host capability like DomParser: the extension uses DOMParser, the CLI linkedom. Update docs/01 and docs/05 in the same change.
acceptance_criteria: Both hosts turn policy HTML into markdown with headings preserved; core never imports readability.

title: M5: heading-aware chunking, sized from real token counts
description: docs/05 stage 4. Split on headings first, then by token count, ~10% overlap, each chunk carrying its heading path. Sizing must come from a real tokenizer, not the chars/4 estimate the WebLLM adapter returns — docs/04 flags underestimating here as overflowing the context window. Chunks should be sized near the limit: S2 showed prefill cost is worse than linear, but more chunks repay the prompt overhead each time.
acceptance_criteria: A long policy chunks to sizes that fit the model's context with margin; heading paths are preserved; overlap does not duplicate whole clauses.

title: M5: discover policy URLs
description: docs/05 stage 1: candidates from PageSnapshot.links policyHint plus common paths on the same registrable domain. Deduplicated, and never off the audit's allowed domains.
acceptance_criteria: A snapshot with a privacy link yields it first; candidates on other registrable domains are excluded.

title: M5: TosReport and Clause schemas
description: docs/05 sections 5 and 8: ClauseCategory, Clause, ClauseExtraction, TosReport. Types next to their zod schema per CLAUDE.md.
acceptance_criteria: Schemas parse the labelled fixtures; a clause with an over-long quote is rejected.

title: M4: explainFinding
description: docs/03 and docs/11: the model writes the explanation field for a finding, given its evidence. The only field a model ever writes. Page-controlled evidence goes into the prompt inside a delimited data block and the output is schema-validated before it touches a Finding (docs/12 T1).
acceptance_criteria: An explained finding validates against FindingSchema; injected instructions in evidence do not change the shape of what comes back.

title: M4: RecordingProvider and replay mode
description: docs/04: a ModelProvider wrapper that records every call to an AuditTrace and a replay provider that answers from a recording. Pure core, no host APIs. This is how the agent loop is tested in CI, which has no GPU (hard rule 6). Requests must key deterministically so replay is exact.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded run replays green in Node with no model present; an unrecorded request fails loudly rather than silently returning nothing.

title: M4: WebLLM adapter must treat an interrupted engine as dead
description: Spike S2: interruptGenerate() stops generation in 280-520ms but leaves the engine returning empty content with finish_reason 'abort' for every subsequent request. resetChat() does not recover it; reload() does not either, and in the Web Worker engine the next call after a reload throws 'Message error should not be 0'. Only discarding the engine and its worker and constructing a new one recovers: 5.2s for 0.5B, 12.4s for 1.5B with weights cached. Reproduced interrupting from inside the consumer loop and from a timer, awaited and not, in a worker and on the main thread. The provider should mark the engine dead on interrupt and rebuild lazily on the next call, so the agent loop never sees a half-working engine.
acceptance_criteria: A cancelled run followed by a new completion succeeds without the caller knowing an engine was rebuilt.

title: M4: pin SRI integrity hashes for the models we ship
description: docs/12 T7 is currently unmitigated. WebLLM ships ModelIntegrity/verifyIntegrity with onFailure:'error', but spike S2 found 0 of 163 prebuilt models carry an integrity field, so weights and the model library are downloaded and executed unverified. Compute hashes for the models we actually offer and supply them through a custom appConfig. Cover model_lib as well as the weights: it is the WASM, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com rather than HuggingFace, and it is executable code rather than data.
acceptance_criteria: A tampered weight or model_lib file fails the load loudly; the README's SRI claim becomes true again.

title: M3: vendor the Observatory analyzer
description: Copy src/analyzer into packages/core/src/analyzers/headers/vendor/ under MPL-2.0 with the licence file, applying the three prunes S1 established (docs/03): hsts.js takes an injected preload map, subresource-integrity.js and redirection.js are dropped. Vendor JS stays out of tsconfig.
acceptance_criteria: The nine tests run from core and return Observatory verdicts; no server dependency is in the graph.

title: M3: headers analyzer and mapping.ts
description: Our own MIT mapping from vendor output to Finding: ruleId, severity, evidence, and the library's own reference links. Builds the axios-shaped Requests object from one worker fetch, including the verified:true assumption S1 documented. Never throws on a single failed test (docs/03).
acceptance_criteria: Header findings appear on fixtures; tests assert expected ruleIds and severities.

title: M2: background worker — cookies, fetch, routing
description: docs/07 and docs/08. chrome.cookies.getAll for flags; cross-origin fetch enforcing the audit's allowed-domain list on its own authority, not the caller's claim (docs/12 T2); routes snapshot.build to the content script. No analysis logic; stays short-lived.
acceptance_criteria: A fetch for a domain outside the allowlist is refused with domain-not-allowed, asserted by a test of the check itself.

title: M2: messaging envelope and zod schemas
description: docs/07: { id, type, payload } envelope, replies echoing replyTo, and the error shape with codes invalid-message, domain-not-allowed, fetch-failed, no-active-tab, capture-failed. Validated with zod at both ends (hard rule 2).
acceptance_criteria: A malformed message is rejected with invalid-message rather than reaching a handler.

title: M2: content script builds the snapshot
description: docs/08: call core's pure builder on request only. Supply hashInlineScript via crypto.subtle.digest, which core cannot do itself. Record a limitation rather than failing when something is blocked.
acceptance_criteria: The content script returns a snapshot that validates against PageSnapshotSchema.

title: M1: Finding schema and Analyzer interface
description: docs/03 Finding schema, Severity, AnalyzerContext, Analyzer. Stable finding id as analyzerId:ruleId:hash(evidence) — needs a hash that works in both hosts without Node crypto or SubtleCrypto (hard rule 1).
acceptance_criteria: Two runs over the same snapshot produce identical finding ids.

title: M1: pure snapshot builder
description: buildSnapshot(doc, opts) in core, shared by the content script and CLI fixtures so what ships and what is tested cannot drift (docs/02). Applies the size budget: links truncated to 500, textExcerpt to 20000, with the matching limitation flags.
acceptance_criteria: Builder output validates against PageSnapshot; truncation sets the documented limitation flags.

title: M1: DOM port for the pure snapshot builder
description: core has no DOM lib (hard rule 1), but the snapshot builder must read a document. Define the minimal structural interfaces core needs (DomDocument/DomElement) so the extension can pass a real Document and the CLI can pass linkedom's. Resolve the Document-typing question docs/01 leaves open and update docs/02 in the same change.
acceptance_criteria: A real browser Document satisfies the port, asserted by a type-level test in the extension package.

title: M1: PageSnapshot zod schema
description: docs/02 schema in packages/core/src/snapshot/schema.ts. Types live next to their schema per CLAUDE.md conventions. Includes ScriptRef, FormRef, CookieRef, LinkRef, PageSnapshot, and the limitations enum.
acceptance_criteria: Schema parses all fixtures; a snapshot missing a required field fails with a useful zod error.

title: M0: packages/core skeleton
description: Pure TypeScript package, no host APIs (CLAUDE.md hard rule 1). Placeholder exports for the public surface named in docs/01: audit(), runAnalyzers(), Capabilities, ModelProvider. zod dependency.
acceptance_criteria: core builds to ESM and is importable from both the cli and extension packages.

title: M0: shared TypeScript config, strict mode
description: tsconfig.base.json with strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + exactOptionalPropertyTypes, ESM/NodeNext resolution. Per-package tsconfig.json extending it. Core builds to ESM with declarations.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm -r build emits dist/ for core and cli with .d.ts files.

title: M0: pnpm workspace root
description: Root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, .npmrc, .gitignore, .editorconfig. Workspace covers packages/core, packages/extension, packages/cli. Node 22, pnpm 10.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm install succeeds; pnpm -r exec node -e 'process.exit(0)' resolves all three packages.

title: S2 — spike: WebLLM in an extension side panel
description: Load Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.1-8B in a side panel document. Confirm WebGPU is available in that context. Verify response_format JSON-schema output against a real zod schema. VERIFY THE CANCELLATION API: interruptGenerate() is not in the published API reference and AbortSignal support depends on it. Measure prefill/decode. Gates M4; sets the numbers in docs/05 section 4 and docs/06 budgets.
acceptance_criteria: A side panel page returns schema-valid JSON from both models, generation can be cancelled mid-run, and measured throughput is written into docs/05 and docs/06.
close_reason: Measured on Apple M4/Chrome 152. WebGPU and response_format confirmed; cancellation, connect-src and T7 all corrected. Numbers in docs/05 and docs/06, raw data in evals/results/spike-s2.json.

title: docs/07: delete bridge protocol, write extension runtime + messaging
description: Replace all 85 lines of WS/pairing/close-codes with chrome.runtime messaging between content script, background worker, side panel.

title: docs/09: delete desktop app, write storage + workbench
description: IndexedDB object stores replacing the SQLite schema; full-page workbench tab for dashboard, history, trace view.

title: docs/01: new architecture diagram + decisions table
description: Drop Electron/bridge/SQLite rows; add WebLLM, IndexedDB, extension-host rows with rationale.

title: CLAUDE.md: strengthen hard rule 1, update layout + commands
description: core must run unmodified in Node AND a browser: no Node built-ins, no DOM, no chrome.*. Everything external arrives via Capabilities. Layout: core/extension/cli. Commit scopes: core/extension/cli/docs.

title: Docs: rewrite for extension-first + WebLLM
description: Remove Electron, the localhost bridge, SQLite, and the Ollama/Anthropic providers from the design docs. Replace with an extension-first architecture hosting WebLLM over WebGPU, with a host-agnostic core that receives a Capabilities object. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/recursive-wishing-octopus.md

title: M6: wire the loop into audit() and both hosts
description: audit() gains the agent path so noAgent stops being the only mode. The CLI runs it with --replay; the side panel runs it live.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm scan with --replay runs the full loop; the side panel can run an agent audit.

title: M6: orchestrator system prompt as a reviewable file
description: docs/06: keep it in agent/prompts/orchestrator.md so it can be reviewed as prose rather than read out of a string literal. Must state that page and policy text are untrusted data — as defence in depth, not as the mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: The prompt is a file, loaded at build time, and its content is asserted in a test.

title: M5: labelled policy fixtures
description: docs/05 evals: fixtures/policies/<site>/policy.md plus labels.json listing expected clauses by category and a distinctive substring. Two of them, per docs/11.
acceptance_criteria: Both fixtures load, and the pipeline runs end to end against them in replay.

title: M5: merge, quote verification, and ranking
description: docs/05 stages 6 and 7. Deduplicate near-identical clauses across overlapping chunks, and — the load-bearing part — verify every quote appears in the source text, dropping those that do not. That guards against both hallucination and injected text smuggling in fake clauses. Ranking is deterministic: category weight times concern. The model assesses concern, it does not rank.
acceptance_criteria: A fabricated quote is dropped; duplicates across overlapping chunks collapse to one; ranking is reproducible.

title: M5: policy cache by content hash and model
description: docs/09: cache extraction results keyed by content hash plus model id. S2 makes this load-bearing rather than an optimisation — re-analysing an unchanged policy costs 90-120 seconds on the default model.
acceptance_criteria: A second run over an unchanged policy makes no model calls.

title: M5: clause extraction (map stage)
description: docs/05 stage 5. One schema-constrained model call per chunk. Chunk text inside a delimited data block announced as untrusted (docs/12 T1). Serial, because one engine handles one request at a time and a second means a second copy of the weights in VRAM. Per-chunk progress, because the user is watching a bar.
acceptance_criteria: Extraction returns schema-valid clauses; a chunk containing injected instructions does not change the shape of what comes back.

title: M4: wire explanations into the side panel
description: Render the model-written explanation on each finding, keeping it visually distinct from the deterministic summary the analyzer wrote. A reader should be able to tell which sentences came from a model.
acceptance_criteria: Explanations render, and their provenance is visible in the UI.

title: M4: model manager UI with download progress
description: docs/08 and docs/09: pick a model, show download progress from initProgressCallback, show what is cached, and show engine state. First use pulls gigabytes and it must never be a surprise (docs/12 T7).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a model shows progress and the side panel reports engine state.

title: M4: implement CompletionRequest.signal on top of interruptGenerate
description: Spike S2: WebLLM exposes no AbortSignal anywhere in its API, so docs/04's CompletionRequest.signal cannot be passed through and must be implemented in the adapter — subscribe to the signal, call interruptGenerate, then rebuild the engine per the sibling issue. Note for docs/06: because cancellation costs an engine rebuild, it belongs on the user's stop button, not on per-step budget enforcement, which should work by not starting the next call.
acceptance_criteria: Aborting via signal stops generation and leaves the provider usable.

title: M3: csp analyzer via csp_evaluator
description: docs/03 and docs/10: csp_evaluator (Apache-2.0, zero runtime deps). Maps its findings to our ruleIds with a mapping table in analyzers/csp/mapping.ts.
acceptance_criteria: unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, wildcard sources, and missing object-src/base-uri produce findings with expected ruleIds.

title: M3: HSTS preload list build script
description: conf/hsts-preload.json is not in the Observatory tarball; it is generated at build time. Ship a script that fetches and reduces the Chromium HSTS preload list, and have the headers analyzer inject it. Absent the list, HSTS still works — only the preloaded verdict is unavailable, which must be reported as unknown rather than missing.
acceptance_criteria: The analyzer runs with and without the list; without it, no false 'not preloaded' finding.

title: M2–M6: verify the panel in a browser (needs a human)
description: Everything from M2 to M6 ends in a check that cannot be run from a terminal. Build with 'pnpm --filter extension build', load packages/extension/.output/chrome-mv3 unpacked in Chromium, run 'pnpm serve-fixture', and audit http://localhost:8787/. Expect the ruleIds in fixtures/site/README.md; cookies/cookie-flags-unknown should NOT appear (if it does, the background worker failed to enrich the snapshot). Then audit a real https site and confirm header, CSP, tracker and library findings appear — run the three build-* scripts first or those analyzers report themselves skipped. Press 'Explain findings' (first use downloads ~1.1 GB for Qwen2.5-1.5B), then 'Read the terms', then 'Full audit' which runs the agent loop end to end. Spike S2 could not cover the side panel's own document lifetime, so watch that the panel survives a model load and a multi-minute run.
acceptance_criteria: Findings, model-written explanations, a ToS report with verified quotes, and a full agent audit with a trace all complete in the side panel.

title: M2: IndexedDB AuditStore
description: docs/09: the webaudit database via idb, audits store keyed by id with by-host and by-started indexes. Implements core's AuditStore. History cap with oldest-first eviction.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trips an audit and lists history under fake-indexeddb in vitest.

title: M2: side panel assembles Capabilities and renders findings
description: docs/08: the side panel is the compute host. Assembles Capabilities over the background worker and the IndexedDB store, calls core.audit(snapshot, { noAgent: true }), renders findings grouped by severity with evidence. Header shows the site and a re-audit control.
acceptance_criteria: Findings render grouped by severity; a raw snapshot toggle exists for development.

title: M1: Node Capabilities and the CLI audit command
description: Node implementations of Capabilities in packages/cli: fetch-backed Http, filesystem AuditStore under ./out/, linkedom DomParser, console ProgressSink and Logger, real Clock. Wire up 'webaudit audit <snapshot.json> --no-agent'.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm --filter cli audit fixtures/snapshots/example.json --no-agent prints findings.

title: M1: snapshot fixtures
description: fixtures/snapshots/: a well-configured baseline, a site with many third-party scripts, an http-only site, and a site with a login form (docs/02). Hand-edited files carry the _synthetic suffix.
acceptance_criteria: Every fixture validates against PageSnapshot in a test that globs the directory.

title: M1: policy-presence analyzer
description: docs/03: no detectable privacy policy or terms link. Reads LinkRef.policyHint from the snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests assert ruleId and severity.

title: M1: forms analyzer
description: docs/03: password fields without autocomplete guidance, login forms on http, cross-origin form actions.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests assert ruleId and severity.

title: M1: scripts analyzer
description: docs/03: external scripts without SRI, scripts from unexpected TLDs, excessive inline scripts.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests assert ruleId and severity.

title: M1: cookies analyzer
description: docs/03: missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite, long-lived session cookies. Must report unknown rather than missing when the no-cookie-flags limitation is set (docs/02 principle).
acceptance_criteria: A snapshot with no-cookie-flags produces no false missing-flag findings.

title: M1: transport analyzer
description: docs/03: http protocol, mixed content, forms posting to http. Snapshot-only, no needs.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests assert ruleId and severity, not prose.

title: M1: Capabilities interface and runAnalyzers
description: docs/01 Capabilities with Http, AuditStore, DomParser, ProgressSink, Clock, Logger. The docs sketch these but do not specify them; write the shapes and update docs/01 and docs/09 in the same change (CLAUDE.md: update the doc with the code). runAnalyzers runs registered analyzers in parallel, skips those whose needs are unmet with an info finding, dedupes, sorts by severity.
acceptance_criteria: runAnalyzers emits an info finding naming the unmet need when headers are absent.

title: M0: ESLint and Prettier
description: Flat-config ESLint with typescript-eslint. A boundary rule enforcing hard rule 1: packages/core may not import node builtins, DOM globals, or chrome.*. Prettier for formatting.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm lint passes; a deliberate 'import fs from node:fs' in core fails lint.

title: M0: vitest setup
description: Shared vitest config. Node environment for core and cli. Smoke test per package so the runner is proven before M1 adds real tests.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm -r test passes.

title: M0: packages/extension skeleton (WXT)
description: WXT MV3 project with empty background, content, and sidepanel entrypoints. Manifest permissions per docs/08. Depends on core.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm --filter extension build produces an unpacked MV3 bundle in .output/.

title: M0: packages/cli skeleton
description: Node host. Bin entry, argument parsing stub for 'audit <snapshot.json> --no-agent'. Depends on core via workspace protocol.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm --filter cli build succeeds and the bin runs, printing usage.

title: M1 — core + CLI (no model, no browser)
description: PageSnapshot, Finding, Analyzer, Capabilities. Pure analyzers: transport, cookies, forms, scripts, policy-presence. CLI host with fs store and node:fetch. Three hand-written snapshot fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm cli audit fixtures/snapshots/x.json --no-agent prints findings; tests assert on ruleId and severity, not prose.
close_reason: pnpm scan prints findings from fixtures; analyzer tests assert ruleId and severity

title: M2 — Extension: capture, store, UI shell
description: Content script builds a snapshot via core's pure builder. Background worker adds cookie flags and implements the privileged http capability. IndexedDB store. Side panel renders findings and hosts core.audit().
acceptance_criteria: Open a page, click audit, see real deterministic findings in the side panel.

title: M0 — Scaffold
description: pnpm workspace: core, extension, cli. TS strict, shared tsconfig.base.json, ESLint, Prettier, vitest. CI: install, build, test.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm -r build && pnpm -r test passes on an empty project.
close_reason: pnpm -r build && pnpm -r test pass; CI mirrors the local gate

title: S1 — spike: Observatory vendor viability
description: Copy mdn-http-observatory src/analyzer (hsts.js, cspParser.js, utils.js, tests/) into a vendor dir, prune imports, confirm it runs in a browser bundle with only browser-safe deps (structured-headers, tldts, dayjs, change-case). Fallback: write ~10 header rules from Observatory's published scoring table. Gates M3.
acceptance_criteria: A browser bundle produces header findings from a fixed headers object, with no Fastify/pg/axios in the dependency graph.
close_reason: Viable: 24 modules, 60 kB, one runtime dep; nine tests return correct verdicts. Three prunes documented in docs/03.

title: docs/11: replace roadmap with M0-M8
description: New milestone order; extension arrives only once there is something worth running in it.

title: docs/10: rewrite dependency list
description: Remove electron*/ws/better-sqlite3/ollama/@anthropic-ai/sdk/node-llama-cpp/promptfoo/@mdn/mdn-http-observatory. Add @mlc-ai/web-llm, idb, csp_evaluator (underscore, 1.1.8). Record MPL-2.0 vendor boundary.

title: docs/12: rewrite T3 and T5, add T7 and T8
description: T3: bridge threat gone, replaced by extension context isolation. T5: no secrets at rest. T7: HuggingFace weight download vs no-telemetry rule, mitigated by SRI integrity. T8: wasm-unsafe-eval in extension CSP.

title: docs/04: replace Ollama+Anthropic adapters with WebLLM
description: Interface unchanged. supportsToolCalls:false makes the JSON action protocol the only path. Add model-download progress surface.

title: docs/08: rewrite extension doc as the product
description: Absorbs most of old docs/09. Side panel hosts core.audit() and the WebLLM engine; background worker is privileged-only and short-lived.

title: M7: workbench models and settings views
description: docs/09: list available models with size and context window, show what is cached; budgets, allowed domains and history cap.
acceptance_criteria: Cached models are listed and settings persist in chrome.storage.local.

title: M5: ToS section in the side panel
description: docs/08: top concerns first, then by category, with each clause showing its verbatim quote and where in the policy it came from.
acceptance_criteria: A TosReport renders; quotes are visibly attributed to their source and heading.

title: M4: decide the model set from the measured throughput
description: Spike S2 measured, on an Apple M4: Qwen2.5-0.5B at 40 tok/s decode and ~1400 tok/s prefill; Qwen2.5-1.5B at 20.5 tok/s decode and ~490 tok/s prefill, 31s cold load. Both report a 4096-token context. On the 1.5B a 2.5k-token chunk prefills in about 6s, putting a 40k-token policy at 90-120s of prefill alone. Decide which models to offer, and set the docs/06 budget defaults from these numbers rather than from guesses.
acceptance_criteria: Default model and budget defaults chosen, with the reasoning recorded.

title: M3: tracker database build script and trackers analyzer
description: docs/10: build a JSON subset from DuckDuckGo Tracker Radar (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — non-commercial, downloaded at build time, never vendored) and classify thirdPartyRequests by category. Uses tldts for eTLD+1 and first/third-party classification. The licence must be flagged in the README.
acceptance_criteria: Third-party domains in a fixture are classified; the analyzer reports unknown when the DB is absent.

title: M3: libraries analyzer from retire.js data
description: docs/10: use retire.js data files, not the scanner. Fingerprint vulnerable library versions from script URLs in the snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: A known-vulnerable version in a fixture URL produces a finding naming the CVE or advisory.

title: M2: local fixture site for manual end-to-end checks
description: docs/08 testing: fixtures/site/ with known issues (insecure form, third-party script without SRI, no policy links), served locally, so the extension can be exercised against a real page without auditing someone else's site.
acceptance_criteria: A documented command serves the site; auditing it in the browser produces the expected ruleIds.

title: M1: core audit() entry point
description: audit(snapshot, { capabilities, budget }) returning AuditResult { findings, tosReport, trace } per docs/01. In M1 it runs analyzers only; noAgent is the only supported mode until M6.
acceptance_criteria: audit() with noAgent returns findings and an empty trace, and is covered by a test.

title: M0: CI workflow
description: GitHub Actions: install, build, lint, test on Node 22. No GPU steps — CI never runs live inference (CLAUDE.md hard rule 6).
acceptance_criteria: Workflow file present and valid; steps mirror the local commands in CLAUDE.md.

title: M6 — Agent loop
description: Tools, budgets, orchestrator, trace, JSON action protocol (the only path — WebLLM tool calling is upstream WIP). Injection fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: An end-to-end audit completes within budget, and injection fixtures provably do not alter the tool-call sequence.

title: M5 — ToS pipeline
description: All eight stages. Policy cache keyed by content hash in IndexedDB — load-bearing now, not an optimisation. Quote verification. ToS UI.
acceptance_criteria: A real site yields a TosReport whose quotes all verify against source text.

title: M3 — Headers, CSP, trackers, libraries
description: Vendored Observatory sources wired to the background worker's fetch. csp_evaluator. Tracker DB build script. retire.js data.

title: docs/06: add Capabilities, provider-aware budgets
description: Generalise ToolContext into Capabilities (adds http, dom, progress, clock). Parallel tool calls are a no-op under a single engine. maxWallMs default will not survive a 40k-token policy.

title: docs/03: rewrite headers analyzer + third-party wrapping section
description: Observatory is a Fastify+Postgres server app, not a library. Vendor its MPL-2.0 src/analyzer sources instead. Schema and Analyzer interface unchanged.

title: docs/05: update chunking, serial execution, evals
description: Chunk sizing for ~4k contexts; one engine means serial map stage; promptfoo replaced by in-browser eval runner.

title: M6: consider recording HTTP alongside model calls
description: A recorded agent run replays the model but still makes real network requests, so a recording made against a live site needs that site reachable. The CI fixture works around it by stubbing http (--offline in scripts/record-agent-run.mjs). Recording the whole external boundary would make any run replayable hermetically, including against real sites. Worth doing only if the evals or the workbench need it — it is a new recording layer, not a tweak.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded, and either an http recording layer or a note that stubbing is sufficient.

title: M3: decide whether to add a CORS Origin probe
description: The vendored CORS test's only interesting verdict needs a probe request carrying an Origin header so the server's reflection of it can be observed. The worker sends a plain fetch, so the test is vendored but not wired. Adding the probe means one extra request with a synthetic Origin header — arguably still passive observation of a page we are already fetching, but it is a behaviour change and docs/12 lists active scanning as a non-goal. Needs a decision, not an implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded in docs/03 or docs/12, and the test either wired or the omission documented as permanent.

title: M7 — Workbench and evals
description: Full-page extension tab: dashboard, history, trace view. In-browser eval runner comparing models on labelled policy fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Model comparison results land in evals/results/.

title: S3 — spike: offscreen document lifetime + WebGPU
description: Confirm WebGPU works in a chrome.offscreen document, which reason applies (WORKERS is the closest fit; there is no WebGPU reason), and whether Chrome closes it on idle. Fallback: background service worker with MLC heartbeat keep-alive (WebGPU there needs Chrome 124+, terminates mid-run). Gates M8.
acceptance_criteria: A documented decision on where the runtime lives for background audits, with measured idle-close behaviour.
